🇲🇽💰 <u>AFORE FEES WERE CUT NEARLY IN HALF. HALF THE AFORES ALREADY OUT-EARN 2021</u>

Before the cap, Mexico's pension fund managers charged workers an average 0.98% on their balances. In 2026 it's 0.54%, the lowest since the cap began.

Even so, five of the ten afores (PensionISSSTE, Invercap, Profuturo, Inbursa and Sura) already earn more in real terms than in 2021, El Economista reports with Consar data. State-run PensionISSSTE leads: its January–September net profit is 57% above 2021.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>SHEINBAUM TO INE COUNCILORS: CUT YOUR OWN PAY</u>

"Let them lower their salaries, let the councilors lower them more," President Sheinbaum said at Monday's mañanera, citing the constitutional rule that no public servant may earn more than the president.

INE councilors make 262,634 pesos a month gross. At least 20,416 INE workers earn 15,856 pesos or less, and some module staff and electoral trainers get between 5,700 and 9,000.

By Monday night, INE's Blanca Cruz answered: starting in 2027, no one at the institute will earn more than the president.
banner: INE: COUNCILORS TOLD TO CUT THEIR PAY

🔥🇲🇽 <u>SUPREME COURT LETS A CASINO WALK AWAY FROM A 4.3-BILLION-PESO TAX BILL</u>

On November 9, seven justices refused to take up the case of Juegos del Bajío, a casino operator that got a 4,306-million-peso tax debt annulled in the administrative court. Hacienda documented that the company's defense rested on a forged contract. Only Lenia Batres and Irene Herrerías voted to hear it.

The majority called it res judicata because Norma Piña's old Court had already turned it down. Batres called that "a lie that should be foreign to the practices of the new Court," and noted the case was listed five times since June: "That allowed ample lobbying."

🇲🇽📉 <u>MEXICO CITY: FEWEST OCTOBER HOMICIDES IN 29 YEARS</u>

Mexico City recorded its lowest homicide count for any October in 29 years, Mayor Clara Brugada reported, with high-impact crime falling for a fifth straight month.

Since 2024, violent car theft is down 56% and missing-person reports are down 51%, while locations of missing people are up 64%. The city's prosecutor reported 6,182 arrest warrants served through October, 32% more than in 2024.

"Five consecutive months of historic lows are not a coincidence, they are the result of a strategy that works. (…) Lives are being saved."

🇲🇽⛏️ <u>PASTA DE CONCHOS: FOUR MORE MINERS IDENTIFIED, 36 NOW HAVE THEIR NAMES BACK</u>

The Unified Command at the Coahuila mine confirmed the identities of Agustín Botello Hernández, Jesús Viera Almendáriz, Jorge Arturo Ortega Jiménez and Juan Ramón Barrientos Gloria, killed in the February 2006 explosion. Their families have been notified.

That makes 36 identified out of the 65 who died, and 31 already returned to their families.

Grupo México and the Calderón government sealed off the search in 2007. Recovery only restarted under López Obrador, and the first remains came out in 2024.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>MIGRANTS ARE 0.88% OF MEXICO'S POPULATION AND PRODUCE 1.7% OF ITS GDP</u>

ECLAC's Humberto Soto de la Rosa told a UNAM economics lecture that migrants living in Mexico contribute 1.7% of GDP while making up just 0.88% of the population. The real figure is likely higher, since many of them work in the informal economy.

Mexico is no longer just a corridor. In 2024, 76% of migrants crossing the country were trying to reach the United States. By September 2025, that share had fallen to 28%.

🇲🇽⚡ <u>CHICOASÉN II PASSES THE HALFWAY MARK</u>

President Sheinbaum toured the CFE's Chicoasén II hydroelectric plant in Chiapas on Sunday. It is 51.35% built, El Economista reports.

Three 80 MW turbines will add 240 MW of clean power using water that has already run through the Manuel Moreno Torres plant upstream, so the Grijalva generates twice. Expected reach: 54,241 homes and 184,421 people, plus 250 million pesos in social works for the municipality.

🇲🇽📚 <u>LA ESCUELA ES NUESTRA NOW REACHES 3 OUT OF 4 PUBLIC SCHOOLS</u>

In two years, the program has reached 141,025 of 185,972 schools, a 75.8% coverage rate. The money goes straight to parent committees, with no intermediaries and no contractors.

This year alone, 73,443 school communities have received funds, covering about 8.8 million students: 23.32 billion pesos delivered so far out of nearly 24 billion budgeted.

🇲🇽🇨🇺 <u>IN MADRID, MEXICO REJECTS THE US EMBARGO ON CUBA</u>

At the 30th Ibero-American Summit, Foreign Minister Roberto Velasco, speaking for President Sheinbaum, restated Mexico's historic position against the embargo and the coercive measures Washington imposes on Cuba.

On security, he set out Mexico's four principles with every nation: respect for sovereignty and territorial integrity, shared but differentiated responsibility, mutual trust, and "cooperation without subordination."

He also reminded Spain of 1939, when Lázaro Cárdenas opened Mexico's doors to thousands of Republican refugees.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>UNDER CÓRDOVA, THE INE ALSO PAID THE "COYOTE" SUPPLIERS</u>

The Hernández Casillas network didn't start with Taddei. Contralínea found at least four INE contracts with the same companies under Lorenzo Córdova, now a councilor of the right-wing party Somos.

One of them, INE/ADQ-0022/15, went to Cartonera Plástica for the 2014–2015 election. It was tendered at 9.83 million pesos and ended above 11 million after a 1.44 million-peso add-on signed on April 8, 2015.

Sheinbaum has suggested the ASF audit go back to the 1990s. But sources told Contralínea that auditors in the state electoral bodies are only asking about Taddei's brief term.
